# Architecture Quality Checklist: Fahes Scan Platform Architecture v2

**Purpose**: Validate the requirements-quality of the master architecture spec/plan package
(`spec.md`, `plan.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/`) before this feature proceeds to
`/speckit-tasks` — this checklist tests whether the *requirements are written well*, not whether
an implementation exists or works.
**Created**: 2026-10-07
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: Generated by `/speckit-checklist` based on the master-architecture planning task's own
stated review dimensions (current-state/target-state separation, reuse-vs-rewrite justification,
engine/domain boundaries, long-running/cancellation semantics, authorization-vs-ownership,
environment classification, credentials/sessions, customer-code isolation, active-security safety,
load-test safety, multi-tenancy, evidence/fingerprint provenance, artifact retention, metering,
reverify, readiness integration, migration, observability, and unresolved-decision honesty).
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact.
Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is
satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements
quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Review pass completed 2026-10-07**: all 46 items were evaluated against `spec.md`/`plan.md`/
`data-model.md`/`contracts/` as they stood after the Clarify phase. Four genuine gaps were found
(CHK004, CHK006, CHK034, CHK042) and fixed in `spec.md`/`plan.md` before marking this checklist —
see the inline note on each. 44/46 items pass after those fixes; 2 items (CHK025, CHK038) are
intentionally left unchecked as legitimately deferred to a future child spec, not as unresolved
defects in this package — see their notes below.

## Current-State vs. Target-State Separation

- [x] CHK001 Is every current-architecture claim in `plan.md`'s "Current-State Architecture"
  section attributable to the cited audit document rather than asserted independently? [Traceability, Plan §Current-State Architecture]
- [x] CHK002 Are current-state facts (e.g. "the browser pool is unwired") and target-state
  proposals (e.g. "deploy it as a service") kept in visibly separate statements rather than
  blended into one sentence anywhere in `plan.md`'s Reuse/Extend/New Matrix? [Clarity, Plan §Reuse/Extend/New Matrix]
- [x] CHK003 Does `spec.md` ever state a forward-looking requirement using present tense in a way
  that could be misread as a current-state fact? [Ambiguity, Spec §Functional Requirements] — reviewed: every FR uses "MUST" for forward requirements and the CURRENT STATE prose block is kept separate.

## Current Scan Path Coverage

- [x] CHK004 Are all three current intake modes (URL, repository, archive) individually accounted
  for in the Execution-Class Matrix's `PASSIVE_HTTP`/`SOURCE_STATIC` rows, or only generically
  referenced? [Completeness, Plan §Execution-Class Matrix] — **FIXED**: added an explicit intake-mode-to-execution-class mapping sentence ahead of the matrix.
- [x] CHK005 Is the three-phase worker execution sequence (Performance+Security+SEO, then UI, then
  Testing) explicitly reflected in the Migration Strategy's compatibility-boundary argument, or
  only asserted at a higher level of abstraction? [Completeness, Plan §Migration Strategy]
- [x] CHK006 Does the spec package state, for the existing AI layer (one call per module,
  labelled-segment assembly), which bounded context owns it going forward, or is this left
  implicit? [Gap, Plan §Bounded Contexts] — **FIXED**: added an explicit "AI Interpretation" row to the Bounded Contexts table.
- [x] CHK007 Are the existing readiness and reverify mechanisms each given their own explicit
  Reuse/Extend classification, rather than one combined classification that could hide a
  difference between the two? [Clarity, Plan §Reuse/Extend/New Matrix]
- [x] CHK008 Is the existing credit-ledger debit/refund mechanism's reconciliation guarantee
  (Constitution Principle VI) explicitly re-confirmed as unaffected by FR-020's metering extension,
  or only implied? [Clarity, Research §R5]

## Reuse-vs-Rewrite Justification

- [x] CHK009 Does every "NEW SYSTEM" classification in `plan.md`'s Reuse/Extend/New Matrix cite a
  specific reason extension was judged insufficient, rather than a general preference for a fresh
  design? [Traceability, Plan §Reuse/Extend/New Matrix]
- [x] CHK010 Is the specific evidence that the existing capability-SDK contract (`AuditCapability`)
  is extensible rather than replaceable documented anywhere the reader does not have to infer it
  from the existing capabilities' source alone? [Gap, Research §R2]
- [x] CHK011 For the one subsystem explicitly marked "NOT REUSABLE for this purpose" (the k6
  harness), is the boundary between "reusable mechanism" and "unreusable assumption" stated
  precisely, or does the classification read as a blanket rejection? [Clarity, Plan §Reuse/Extend/New Matrix]

## Execution Engine / Product Domain Boundary

- [x] CHK012 Does `plan.md`'s Target Architecture diagram or the Engine Contracts Summary ever show
  a product domain with a direct dependency that bypasses an engine (i.e., a domain owning its own
  private measurement logic)? [Consistency, Contracts §engine-contracts-summary.md] — reviewed: no domain row bypasses an engine.
- [x] CHK013 Is it explicitly specified what happens when two domains need the same engine at
  different concurrency/timeout profiles, or is this left as an unstated assumption? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases] — covered by spec.md's Edge Cases bullet on engine contention.
- [x] CHK014 Are the "Does NOT own" columns in the Engine Contracts Summary populated for every
  engine, or do any rows leave this column implicit/blank? [Completeness, Contracts §engine-contracts-summary.md]

## Long-Running Execution, Cancellation, and the Three-Way Stop Distinction

- [x] CHK015 Does the Execution-Class Matrix specify a distinct cancellation behavior for every one
  of the nine classes, or do any rows inherit a generic "existing" value without stating what that
  means for a stateful, long-running class? [Completeness, Plan §Execution-Class Matrix]
- [x] CHK016 Is the difference between user cancellation, platform emergency stop, and
  target-safety kill switch (FR-022) defined with enough specificity that a future child spec could
  determine which one applies to a given failure scenario, or only at the level of naming the three
  categories? [Measurability, Spec §FR-022]
- [x] CHK017 Are idempotence requirements specified for every execution class that may be retried,
  or does FR-018/the Runtime/Queue Model leave idempotence as an assumption for classes other than
  the ones explicitly discussed? [Gap, Plan §Runtime / Queue Model] — covered by Constitution Principle XII's "idempotence MUST be proven, not assumed" default-to-`attempts:1` rule, which applies platform-wide.

## Authorization vs. Ownership Verification

- [x] CHK018 Is there any requirement anywhere in `spec.md` or `plan.md` that could be satisfied by
  Ownership Verification alone for an execution class other than `PASSIVE_HTTP`/`SOURCE_STATIC`/
  `BROWSER`/`CRAWLER`? [Conflict, Plan §Safety & Authorization Model] — reviewed: none found.
- [x] CHK019 Does the Authorization/safety decision flow diagram define a refusal path for every
  combination of missing Authorization, unclassified Environment, and out-of-Scope request, or
  only for some combinations? [Coverage, Plan §Target Architecture]
- [x] CHK020 Is "explicit, separately-granted" (FR-004) defined precisely enough to distinguish it
  from an implicit grant inferred from another field, or could a future child spec read this
  requirement as satisfiable by inference? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004]

## Environment Classification (Production vs. Staging)

- [x] CHK021 Is it explicitly stated what happens when a Target has no `TargetEnvironment`
  classification at all (unclassified), or does the spec only address the classified case?
  [Gap, Data-Model §TargetEnvironment] — `data-model.md` states unclassified MUST be treated as refusing any Environment-restricted class.
- [x] CHK022 Does any requirement anywhere allow an Environment classification to widen what an
  existing Authorization grant covers, which would contradict FR-002/Constitution Principle X?
  [Conflict, Spec §FR-002] — reviewed: none found.

## Credentials and Session Isolation

- [x] CHK023 Is the distinction between `CredentialBinding` (target-testing credential) and the
  existing GitHub OAuth token vault (platform-integration credential) stated clearly enough that a
  future child spec could not confuse the two, or does the wording risk ambiguity? [Clarity, Data-Model §CredentialBinding]
- [x] CHK024 Are session-isolation requirements (no reuse across scans or tenants) stated as a
  testable constraint on `SessionBinding`'s lifetime, or only as a general principle without a
  concrete enforcement point? [Measurability, Data-Model §SessionBinding]

## Customer-Code Isolation (Constitution Principle XI)

- [ ] CHK025 Does `plan.md` specify, for the `SOURCE_EXECUTION` class, what evidence would be
  required to demonstrate a future isolation mechanism meets the "no known escape path" bar, or is
  this left entirely to the future child spec with no acceptance criterion at all? [Gap, Plan §Execution-Class Matrix] — **INTENTIONALLY DEFERRED**: the constitution's own `TODO(UNTRUSTED_EXECUTION_MECHANISM)` explicitly assigns the mechanism choice (and therefore its acceptance bar) to that future child spec's `/speckit-plan`; inventing a concrete criterion here without evidence would itself violate the "do not invent an answer" instruction this review operates under. Flagged for `/speckit-analyze` and the Open Decisions list, not silently resolved.
- [x] CHK026 Is the reasoning for why the existing sandbox-runner's process-level permission model
  is insufficient for customer-code execution specific to this platform's evidence, or does it read
  as a generic "containers are safer" assertion? [Clarity, Research §R4]

## Active-Security Safety (Constitution Principle X)

- [x] CHK027 Does the Execution-Class Matrix's `ACTIVE_SECURITY` row specify budgets (request,
  concurrency, duration) with enough precision that a future child spec has a concrete starting
  point, or only that budgets "exist"? [Measurability, Plan §Execution-Class Matrix]
- [x] CHK028 Is the requirement that production is never a default-permitted environment for
  `ACTIVE_SECURITY` stated as an explicit MUST, or could it be read as a recommendation? [Clarity, Plan §Execution-Class Matrix]

## Load-Test Safety and Internal-vs-Customer-Facing Distinction

- [x] CHK029 Is the distinction between the existing internal-only k6 harness and the proposed
  `LOAD_CAPACITY` engine stated with a concrete, checkable difference (e.g. target selection, auth
  model), or only as a categorical label? [Clarity, Plan §Reuse/Extend/New Matrix]
- [x] CHK030 Are safety requirements for `LOAD_CAPACITY` (immediate stop on signal, staging-only
  default) stated with the same rigor as `ACTIVE_SECURITY`'s, or is this class under-specified by
  comparison? [Consistency, Plan §Execution-Class Matrix]

## Multi-Tenancy

- [x] CHK031 Does every new entity in `data-model.md` state its tenant-scoping key explicitly, or
  do any entities (e.g. `ScopeDefinition`, `ScanProfile`) leave scoping unstated because they are
  not directly tenant-owned? [Completeness, Data-Model §all sections] — reviewed: `ScopeDefinition`/`ScanProfile` are correctly unscoped templates referenced by scoped entities (`TargetAuthorization`), not directly tenant data themselves.
- [x] CHK032 Is the requirement that a new storage location's retention/cleanup path must be
  "resolved, not inherited" (Constitution Principle XIII) specific enough to be checked against a
  future child spec, or does it rely on the reviewer's judgment with no stated check? [Measurability, Constitution §XIII]

## Evidence Provenance and Fingerprint Identity

- [x] CHK033 Does `data-model.md`'s `Evidence` entity specify validation rules for when
  `inlinePayload` vs. `artifactId` is required, or is this left as "determined by the foundation
  child spec" with no interim criterion? [Gap, Data-Model §Evidence] — correctly and explicitly deferred to that foundation spec, with the deferral itself stated rather than silently assumed.
- [x] CHK034 Is the requirement that every engine "MUST produce findings identifiable by a stable
  fingerprint" (FR-016) accompanied by any criterion for what counts as a valid fingerprint
  computation for a genuinely new evidence kind (e.g. a load-test metric), or does it only restate
  the existing mechanism without addressing the new case? [Gap, Spec §FR-016] — **FIXED**: FR-016 now explicitly separates the binding mechanism requirement from the engine-specific `fingerprintParts` content question.

## Artifact Storage and Retention

- [x] CHK035 Does the Artifact retention requirement explicitly reference closing the known staged-
  upload retention gap, or could a future child spec satisfy "same as report retention" while still
  leaving that specific gap open? [Conflict, Data-Model §Artifact] — FR-015 explicitly calls out closing this gap by name.
- [x] CHK036 Is "same retention policy and timing as today's report data" (the 2026-10-07
  Clarification) specific enough to be implemented without further clarification, or does it
  assume the reader already knows the exact report-retention sweep's parameters? [Clarity, Spec §Clarifications] — acceptable: the parameters themselves (`enforceRetention`) are existing, documented code the owning foundation spec will read directly; this master spec correctly does not restate them.

## Metering / Cost Extension

- [x] CHK037 Is the narrow metering scope (FR-020) stated as an exhaustive list (only
  `LOAD_CAPACITY` and `SOURCE_EXECUTION`), or does any other requirement in the package imply a
  third class might also need metering without updating FR-020? [Consistency, Spec §FR-020] — reviewed: no other requirement implies a third metered class.
- [ ] CHK038 Does the plan specify what happens if a future child spec discovers a flat-priced class
  has become genuinely cost-unbounded, beyond "MAY revisit with new evidence" — is there a stated
  process, or is this a dead end for that child spec? [Gap, Spec §FR-020] — **INTENTIONALLY DEFERRED**: the escalation *process* for amending a Clarifications-session decision (who approves it, what evidence threshold applies) is a governance-process question for Fahes's own product/engineering leadership, not an architecture question this spec can answer from repository evidence. Flagged for the Open Decisions list rather than invented.

## Reverify Strategy per Execution Class

- [x] CHK039 Does FR-018 specify a reverify approach for every one of the nine execution classes, or
  only for a subset, leaving the rest to be inferred? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018] — cross-checked against the Execution-Class Matrix's Reverify column, which fills all nine.
- [x] CHK040 Is "preserve the valuable targeted-single-finding concept... wherever the execution
  class allows it" (FR-018) specific enough to determine, for any given class, whether it allows it
  or not — or is this left to case-by-case judgment with no stated test? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-018] — the Execution-Class Matrix's per-row Reverify column makes this determination concretely for all nine classes, resolving the abstract wording in FR-018 itself.

## Readiness Integration

- [x] CHK041 Is the requirement that readiness "continues to consume normalized... outcomes rather
  than hardwiring any engine's implementation details" (FR-019) accompanied by a concrete example
  of what "hardwiring" would look like, so a reviewer can recognize a violation, or is the
  prohibition stated only in the abstract? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019] — the Runtime/Queue Model and Bounded Contexts sections of `plan.md` give the concrete positive example (readiness consumes `ModuleType`-keyed scores, never an engine-specific field), which makes the abstract prohibition checkable by contrast.

## Migration and Backward Compatibility

- [x] CHK042 Does FR-024's "strict parallel-run, no cutover window, ever" apply unambiguously to
  every future child spec, or could a child spec argue its change is not a "cutover" under some
  narrower reading? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-024] — **FIXED**: FR-024 now explicitly enumerates that pricing, schema, contract, and UI changes are all included, closing the narrow-reading loophole.
- [x] CHK043 Is the compatibility boundary ("a plan containing only PASSIVE_HTTP/SOURCE_STATIC
  classes is indistinguishable from today's behavior") stated as a testable claim, or only as an
  architectural assertion with no verification method named? [Measurability, Plan §Migration Strategy] — SC-004's `git diff`-based verification method makes this testable at the planning-pass level; each child spec's own plan is required (FR-025) to repeat an equivalent additive-only demonstration.

## Observability Without Leakage

- [x] CHK044 Does FR-023 specify a concrete rule for determining whether a given observability
  field could expose a secret/payload, or does it rely entirely on reviewer judgment per future
  child spec? [Gap, Spec §FR-023] — acceptable: FR-023 names the specific fields allowed (duration, queue wait, resource usage, failures/retries, cancellation, cost, request counts, health) as an enumerated allow-list, which functions as the concrete rule (anything not on the list, especially raw payload/credential content, defaults to excluded).

## Unresolved Decisions Honesty

- [x] CHK045 Does the spec package contain any requirement that reads as settled but is actually
  contingent on one of the explicitly-deferred TODOs in the constitution amendment
  (`TODO(ACTIVE_SECURITY_AUTHORIZATION_MODEL)`, `TODO(UNTRUSTED_EXECUTION_MECHANISM)`) without
  cross-referencing that TODO? [Conflict, Constitution §Sync Impact Report] — reviewed: CHK025 above is the one place this risk existed, and it is now explicitly cross-referenced rather than silently settled.
- [x] CHK046 Are all four Clarifications from the 2026-10-07 session reflected consistently
  everywhere their topic recurs in `spec.md` and `plan.md`, or does any section still read as if
  the earlier placeholder/unresolved framing still applies? [Consistency, Spec §Clarifications] — cross-checked: FR-004/FR-015/FR-020/FR-024 and their corresponding `plan.md` sections (Safety Model, Execution-Class Matrix's cost column, Migration Strategy) all carry the post-Clarification wording.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers — not
  applicable to this feature since `/speckit-implement` is intentionally not run for a master
  architecture spec, but the convention is preserved for consistency with every other feature.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify`
  and `/speckit-clarify`; this file does not alter or duplicate that one.
- Items are numbered sequentially (CHK001-CHK046) for easy reference during `/speckit-analyze`.
- CHK025 and CHK038 remain unchecked by design — both are carried forward into `decisions.md`'s
  Open Decisions section as `PRODUCT DECISION REQUIRED`/deferred-to-child-spec items, not silently
  dropped.
- **Addendum (post-Analyze independent review, 2026-10-07)**: FR-027 and FR-028 (evidence
  redaction for active/adversarial/authenticated classes; artifact size budgets) were added after
  this checklist's own review pass, found by the mandatory independent adversarial self-review
  that follows `/speckit-analyze`. They do not require renumbering this checklist — both are
  additive to the existing Evidence/Artifact requirements this checklist already reviewed (CHK033,
  CHK035) and are consistent with those items' findings, not in tension with them. See
  `decisions.md` ADR-009.
